title: Detecting functions at punctured-spectrum germs
statement: Let A be a Noetherian commutative local ring of depth at least two. If a in A has zero germ at each point of Spec A other than the closed point, under the canonical affine global-section identification, then a=0. Zero germs mean zero in the local rings, not merely residue fields.

source.place: Tags 0311 and 00LL: localization detection at associated primes and regular elements avoiding associated primes

proof.text: The maximal ideal cannot be associated: an associated maximal ideal contains only zerodivisors, so every regular sequence in it is empty. Nakayama gives the properness required in the depth definition, and hence depth zero, contradicting the hypothesis.

For each associated prime p use the zero-germ assumption at its nonclosed point and the canonical stalk localization isomorphism to obtain a/1=0 in A_p. The localization zero criterion gives s outside p with s*a=0. Detection by localizations at associated primes gives a=0.

lean.statement:
theorem eq_zero_of_depth_two_punctured_germs
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsLocalRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (hdepth : (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := A) A)
    (a : A)
    (ha : ∀ x : Spec (.of A), x ≠ IsLocalRing.closedPoint A →
      ((Spec (.of A)).presheaf.Γgerm x).hom ((ΓSpecIso (.of A)).inv.hom a) = 0) :
    a = 0
